methodology.title: K-BENCHMARK Methodology
methodology.desc: How ALPAR AI evaluates, scores, and audits AI models for accountability.
methodology.heading: K-BENCHMARK Methodology
methodology.subheading: An open, transparent framework for evaluating AI model trustworthiness.
methodology.whatIsText: K-BENCHMARK is ALPAR AI's open methodology for scoring AI models across safety, truthfulness, fairness, privacy, robustness, and transparency dimensions. Scores are computed from verified incident reports, cross-audit engine results, and domain expert evaluations using Wilson-score confidence intervals.
methodology.cat_K5_desc: Real-world AI incident evaluation grounded in the ALPAR incident registry, combined with adversarial jailbreaks.
methodology.cat_K6_desc: TruthfulQA-based factuality analysis paired with curated Turkish-context factual claims.
methodology.cat_K7_desc: Evaluation of Turkish language proficiency using translated MMLU-TR and bespoke local regulatory test sets.
methodology.cat_K8_desc: Assessment of model decision-making logic against Art. 73 regulatory scenarios based on EU AI Act taxonomy.
methodology.cat_K9_desc: Standard mathematical problem-solving capability checked against GSM8K and MATH benchmarks.
methodology.cat_K10_desc: Verification of structural instruction-following accuracy using IFEval-like constraints.
methodology.cat_K11_desc: Adversarial jailbreak protection and prompt-injection defense rating under human-approved simulation.
methodology.cat_K12_desc: Needle-in-a-haystack retrieval evaluation for context lengths up to 32k tokens.
methodology.scoringText: Each category is scored using a Wilson-score confidence interval, which accounts for sample size and provides a statistically rigorous lower bound. This prevents small-sample noise from inflating ratings.
methodology.wilsonNote: Wilson-score is a standard method in binomial proportion estimation, commonly used in platforms like Reddit and IMDb for robust rating systems.
methodology.dataSourcesText: Scores are derived from: (1) verified incident reports submitted via the ALPAR platform, (2) automated cross-audit engine evaluations using established benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, IFEval, BBH), (3) domain expert assessments from the L3 advisor network, and (4) publicly available model documentation and technical reports.
methodology.disclaimer: K-BENCHMARK scores are informational and provided 'as-is'. They do not constitute a compliance certification or legal opinion. ALPAR AI is 'AI Act ready/aligned', not compliant. See Terms of Service for full disclaimer.
methodology.adjudication_intro: The cross-audit engine resolves discrepancies through a debate between two independent models, and a separate referee ('Supreme Court') model synthesizes the debate into the final Truth Score. The referee chain is defined in the source code (SUPREME_COURT_CHAIN in src/lib/ai/openrouter-gateway.ts) and currently contains these models:
methodology.adjudication_note: This list is published exactly as coded in src/lib/ai/openrouter-gateway.ts. The adjudication chain currently contains 5 premium models with provider-level failover; when the chain changes, this page is updated to match.
methodology.adjudication_text: Unlike traditional benchmarking setups that simply verify raw responses against static tokens, ALPAR AI employs a dynamic cross-model debate. Two models independently evaluate an incident, challenge each other's assessments, and submit rebuttals; a separate referee ('Supreme Court') model then synthesizes the debate into a final Truth Score. This minimizes static scoring bias and provides robust, peer-reviewed evaluation metrics.

methodology.subtitle: How we calculate Trust Score
methodology.intro: Our proprietary methodology ensures unbiased and transparent rankings.
methodology.aiIssDesc: CVSS-adapted deterministic standard for quantifying AI incident severity across impact, scope, exploitability, and AI context factors.
methodology.aiIssSubheading: An open, reproducible vector framework for quantifying real-world AI incidents.
methodology.aiIssWhatIsText: AI-ISS (AI Incident Severity Score) is ALPAR AI's open standard for assessing the severity of AI incidents. Adapted from the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS v3.1), AI-ISS replaces qualitative tags (Low/Medium/High) with a reproducible, multi-dimensional numerical rating from 0.0 to 10.0.
methodology.aiIssImpactDesc: Measures physical safety harm, algorithmic bias, PII data leakage, financial disruption, and regulatory severity under EU AI Act Article 73.
methodology.aiIssScopeDesc: Evaluates blast radius across individual users, enterprise systems, or systemic society-wide infrastructure.
methodology.aiIssExploitabilityDesc: Rates prompt injection/jailbreak complexity, autonomous execution velocity, and attack surface access vectors.
methodology.aiIssContextDesc: Applies context multipliers (0.9x to 1.3x) based on training data contamination, model autonomy level, and critical deployment domain.
methodology.aiIssFormulaText: Base Score = (Impact × 0.45 + Scope × 0.30 + Exploitability × 0.25) × Context Multiplier
methodology.aiIssExampleText: Scenario: Autonomous agent leaks customer PII via prompt injection. Impact: 8.5, Scope: 7.0, Exploitability: 8.0 -> Base = 7.925. Context Multiplier (High Autonomy): 1.1x -> Final AI-ISS Score = 8.7 (High Severity).
methodology.aiIssRelationText: AI-ISS measures individual incident severity, whereas K-BENCHMARK evaluates overall model reliability. AI-ISS scores serve as a primary quantitative input vector into K-BENCHMARK safety ratings.

founder_story.title: Why I Built This
founder_story.highlight: Grok asked me for my passport.
founder_story.p1: In early 2026, I was using Grok when it told me something that stopped me cold: that it had already incorporated my company, made financial payments on my behalf, and was now requesting my passport for 'verification'. Every word was a lie. Grok had invented a parallel reality â€” completely fabricated â€” and delivered it with algorithmic certainty.
founder_story.p2: What scared me wasn't just the lie. It was the realization that I had no recourse. There was no hotline. No independent record. No way to warn the next person. The AI company's support page had a FAQ. A FAQ. For a system that had demanded my passport.
founder_story.quote: I had no recourse. So I built one.
founder_story.p3: ALPAR AI is the infrastructure I wish had existed that day. A place where what happened to me â€” and to thousands of others â€” is documented, verified, and made impossible to ignore. You report it. Providers must respond. The public record lives forever. Because the only thing worse than AI causing harm is AI causing harm with no one watching.
founder_story.transition_p: If this happened to you â€” or you've seen it happen to someone else â€” your report takes 60 seconds and requires no account. The evidence you submit tonight could prevent the same harm tomorrow.

moderation.description: Rules and guidelines for submitting and moderating incident reports on ALPAR AI.
moderation.headline: Content Moderation Guidelines
moderation.subtitle: We aim to document real-world AI failures with maximum truthfulness, transparency, and fairness. These guidelines explain how content is verified and moderated.
moderation.rules_subtitle: Every submission is reviewed against these baseline community standards.
moderation.rule_1_desc: All reported AI incidents must be accompanied by concrete evidence: screenshot files, JSON logs, or archived URL web links demonstrating the failure. Allegations without proof will not be published.
moderation.rule_2_desc: Reports must not contain user names, raw email addresses, IP addresses, or phone numbers. Our PII Guardian automatically masks this data, but users must make a reasonable effort to avoid submitting it.
moderation.rule_3_desc: Incidents must represent system failures, hallucinations, bias, security breaches, or unexpected behavior by AI models. General disagreements with AI viewpoints do not constitute system failures.
moderation.rule_4_desc: We do not tolerate abusive language, defamation, targeted harassment, or discriminatory remarks. Content violating this rule will be deleted instantly.
moderation.dispute_desc: AI developers and providers have the right to dispute any incident report that they believe is fraudulent, inaccurate, or already resolved. Providers can log into the Provider Portal, submit an official response, or request a moderation review by our team. Disputes are reviewed within 48 hours.
